body:
WHAT
Every line that tells the user what the deletion guard and OVERDRIVE do says what the permission engine really does in that stance.
- The engine's status line when the deletion guard is switched (set_deletion_guard), which the desktop re-sends on every session start: on → "deletion guard on — destructive calls ask; OVERDRIVE turns this off (nothing asks there)"; off → "deletion guard off — deletions run without asking (deleting a .magentra state folder still asks, outside OVERDRIVE)". The same line is true in both stances, because on a link the desktop sends set_deletion_guard before set_overdrive.
- The /overdrive lines name the kill-by-name exception: on → "⚡ OVERDRIVE engaged — nothing asks (deletions, .magentra and .env edits, writes outside the workspace all run; a kill by process name is refused instead), and the turn self-verifies before it ends."; off → "OVERDRIVE disengaged — deletions, edits to .magentra/.env and kills by process name ask again; turns end without the self-verify pass."
- The desktop footer hint: outside OVERDRIVE "runs commands · deletions ask" or "runs commands · deletions allowed"; in OVERDRIVE "autonomous · nothing asks".
- The desktop glossary: "deletion guard — destructive commands ask first unless Deletions is set to ALLOW above. OVERDRIVE turns it off: nothing asks there." and a new entry "process-kill guard — a command that stops processes by name (taskkill /IM, pkill, killall, Stop-Process -Name) asks first; in OVERDRIVE it is refused, because it would stop every matching process on this computer."

WHY
Field test 2026-09-23, finding S-02. At start the engine said "deletion guard on — destructive calls always ask"; at 18:45:12 and 18:52:40 the agent ran rm -f with no prompt (transcript: source mode). OVERDRIVE turns the deletion guard off by design (permissions.ts: "OVERDRIVE turns both off: it means nothing asks, literally"; deletion-guard's own test proves it). The desktop said the same false thing in two more places: the glossary ("always ask first — even in OVERDRIVE") and the footer ("autonomous · deletions always ask"). Outside OVERDRIVE the footer said "asks before commands", although commands have not asked since the stance default became allow (2026-07-26).

WHERE
engine/core/src/runtime/engine.ts — the set_deletion_guard case in the request handler, and the overdrive case in handleSlash. app/renderer/modules/state.js — renderSafetyHint(). app/renderer/index.html — the GLOSSARY card.

TEST CHECKLIST
1. (fs) In a real engine (scripted provider), for the deletion guard on and off, each with OVERDRIVE on and off: the status line printed when the guard is set agrees with what a real deletion then does in that engine. Where the deletion runs unasked, the line does not say it always asks and names the reason (OVERDRIVE, or the guard is off); where it asks, the line says it asks. The /overdrive on line names the kill-by-name refusal.
2. (ui) In the real app, the footer hint in OVERDRIVE says nothing asks and does not say deletions ask; outside OVERDRIVE it does not say commands ask. The glossary's deletion-guard entry says OVERDRIVE turns it off, and a process-kill guard entry exists.
